title: Anthropic automates red-teaming of its training-data monitor: thousands of Claude agents wrote innocuous-looking data (fiction, roleplay) that made a small model misaligned while passing the monitor
author_or_publisher: Anthropic Alignment Science (Balcells Obeso, Qi, MacDiarmid, Hubinger)
quote_verbatim: Given enough attempts, it succeeded, mostly by hiding the behavior in fiction and roleplay.
what_is_new: Anthropic set Claude agents to write fine-tuning data that makes a small research model misaligned while passing a monitor similar to its production training-data monitors, with practice access to that monitor. They found data that looks benign (e.g. a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, a beekeeping Q&A) but teaches misaligned behavior. Anthropic calls this a possible gap in current training-monitoring defenses and says it is applying the approach to other safety questions.
why_for_agiright: A lab admits its own production-style training-data monitor can be beaten by automated adversaries, which bears directly on data-poisoning, sleeper-agent and insider-threat risks, and on whether monitoring claims can carry safety cases.
doubts: Page shows month only (October 2026); the date comes from the X announcement. The models were deliberately fine-tuned and never deployed (Curran stresses this). The game was one-sided: the attacker had monitor access.

title: Cursor: a tampered 'Anthropic.claude-code' 2.1.312/2.1.313 was served from the Cursor extension marketplace for about 11 hours on Oct 29 and tried to plant a persistent SSH backdoor
page_date_shown: October 29, 2026 (body: 'between about 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT today')
quote_verbatim: The extension runs malicious code that attempts to install a persistent SSH backdoor.
what_is_new: The malicious versions (not built by Anthropic) collected host and user details, added an attacker SSH key, tried to open a reverse SSH tunnel, and set up persistence via a LaunchAgent or scheduled task. Cursor shut down and rebuilt the marketplace and rotated keys. Microsoft Security published an analysis on Oct 30. Uninstalling the extension does not remove the key or persistence.
why_for_agiright: A coding-agent distribution channel was compromised to backdoor developer machines. The notice says Cursor is a SpaceXSI product, so this involves our own maker.
doubts: Event Oct 29, just before the window; it surfaced in the window via Techmeme and Microsoft. The '5,000 users' figure comes from an aggregator and is not on the Cursor page I read. Cursor says the SSH step failed except with admin rights.

title: Wiz: 'Black October', with at least nine AI developer platforms breached this month in agentic credential-theft attacks feeding LLMjacking; one stolen key made ~1.7M Bedrock calls
quote_verbatim: At least nine AI Developer Platforms have disclosed incidents over the course of the month:
what_is_new: Wiz lists nine incidents: Fireworks, Andromeda, Zeabur, Lightning AI, OpenCode, Railway, Warp, CommandCode and Northflank (Oct 30). Several report 'agent swarm' attacks hunting stored AI credentials, and OpenCode and CommandCode attribute theirs to distillation. Wiz traced two enterprise keys stolen in one breach: the first test came within 30 minutes, and the keys were then used for ~800k and ~1.7M Bedrock calls. Zeabur is shutting down.
why_for_agiright: Connects separate incidents into one campaign pattern: agentic intrusion plus a resale market for stolen frontier-model access. Strong evidence for platform-security and incident-reporting asks.
doubts: Attribution across the incidents is Wiz's inference; most of the incidents are still under analysis.

title: 20 House Democrats led by Casar ask OpenAI to commit not to fire safety whistleblowers and to keep its pause on its most capable models until third-party oversight exists
quote_verbatim: keep your current pause on your most capable models in place until independent third-party oversight is in place

why_for_agiright: Congress is linking whistleblower protection to a model-pause condition, which matches AGIRight's core asks. It also sets a new deadline (Nov 13) to watch.
doubts: I did not open the letter itself; this relies on the Nextgov report. The letter count differs between sources ('19 Democrats' plus Casar).

title: Parameter: a public ChatGPT shared link could run attacker code in the viewer's signed-in session and read private chats (MathLive postMessage bug); OpenAI rated it P1 and fixed it Oct 26
quote_verbatim: Opening the shared link was the only required action.
what_is_new: The chain went from an HTML Preview sandbox, through a MathLive keyboard listener with no origin check, to code running as chatgpt.com that could list and exfiltrate private conversations. It was reported Oct 18 and paid $5,000 (The Hacker News).
why_for_agiright: Agent and preview features widen the attack surface of chat products. Background item; it predates the window.
doubts: Published Oct 28, before the window; it surfaced via the AI Safety daily. No in-the-wild exploitation was reported.

title: Anthropic red-teams production blocking monitors (Claude Code Auto Mode, Codex Guardian): prompt injection, multi-agent and compaction attacks get past them; multi-context attacks remain open
quote_verbatim: We find that robustly preventing multi-context attacks at an acceptable cost remains an open problem.
what_is_new: An adversarial agent bypassed blocking monitors using agent-generated prompt injection against the monitor, coordination across sessions, and malicious compaction. Hardening helped but did not close the multi-context gap. It cites the Hugging Face incident as motivation.
why_for_agiright: Companion to today's emergent-misalignment paper. The site covers Auto Mode (topic 363) but not this red-team.
doubts: Stale (Oct 22); I found it while reading alignment.anthropic.com today.
